title: AZ affinity misallocation causing reserved pool under-provision and customer burst failures
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Multiple enterprise customers observed repeated burst failures and silent token drops during regional peak windows. Root cause traced to a recent autoscaler change that over-applied AZ affinity multipliers when computing usable headroom for reserved pools. One AZ per region was effectively starved of headroom despite global capacity being available, preventing burst routing and causing customer-facing throttles. Impact included sustained error rates for Dedicated tenants, degraded SLAs, and escalations from two large customers.

Scope: Affects Dedicated reserved pools under the new topology-aware allocation mode when tenant affinity + private-agent-nodes flags are set. Observed in eu-west-1 and us-east-1 clusters. Estimated 7% of Dedicated capacity windows saw degraded performance during the incident window.

Hypothesis: An arithmetic regression multiplied the AZ headroom penalty twice when computing per-tenant reservation weights. This produced artificially low per-AZ allocations and prevented the normal cross-AZ fallback logic from engaging because affinity checks erroneously marked pools as "ineligible" rather than "low headroom."
reproduction_steps: 1) Provision a Dedicated tenant with AZ affinity enabled and private-agent-nodes=true
2) Simulate burst traffic pattern with 20-30x baseline RPS spike for 3 minutes
3) Observe reserved-pool allocator logs: per-AZ headroom reported negative for the affinity AZ while overall region headroom is positive
4) Submit requests and check that routing fails to fallback to compatible pools due to ineligibility flag
telemetry_findings: Autoscaler headroom metric (autoscaler.headroom.per_az) frequently reported -5%..-30% for one AZ while region headroom remained >= 40%
Spike in reserved-pool-declared-ineligible events correlated with customer 5xx rates
KV cache hot-shard persisted in starved AZ leading to coldstarts when fallback should have been used
Deployment times: regression introduced in runtime-2.4.0 -> runtime-2.4.1 path
initial_mitigation: 2026-03-10 14:22 UTC: Emergency policy change — temporarily disabled strict AZ affinity gating for burst routing to allow cross-AZ fallback (rolled via flighted config)
2026-03-10 15:05 UTC: Committed emergency reserved capacity in starved AZ to blunt immediate customer impact
Applied temporary alert: reserved_pool_az_starvation -> P0 runbook triggered and oncall paged
root_cause: A logic regression in topology-aware allocator: when both tenant AZ affinity and private-agent-nodes were true, an AZ penalty multiplier was applied twice due to merging two code paths (affinity_penalty * private_node_penalty) without normalizing for the shared dimension. This caused the allocator to mark pools as ineligible rather than low-headroom, preventing fallback and cross-AZ routing. Additionally, there were no unit/e2e tests covering the combined flag interaction, so the regression escaped CI.
resolution: Patch: Adjust allocation math to apply a single normalized AZ penalty and add guard checks that convert negative headroom into 'low_headroom' state instead of 'ineligible'
2026-03-11 09:40 UTC: Deployed autoscaler hotfix build (git PR #4321) to canary and then to all regions after 30m observation
Rollback not required — patch is additive and guarded, but can be rolled back if unintended side effects observed
Added metric autoscaler.affinity_penalty_applied_count and autoscaler.ineligible_to_low_headroom_counter for future monitoring
code_changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/4321 - fix(allocator): normalize AZ penalty application and safe-state translation

https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2789 - compatibility guard to ensure routing accepts 'low_headroom' as fallback
runbook_updates: Added a playbook step to temporarily lift AZ affinity and force cross-AZ routing for P0 events

2026-03-12 11:00 UTC: Post-incident summary and ETA for permanent fix delivered to customers; offered credits for SLA misses
